h1: The 9 Best Monitor Light Bars for Gaming of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best Gaming Monitor Light Bars: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: 9 monitor light bars for gaming compared on bias lighting, RGB, curved-screen fit and controls, from BenQ to Govee and Razer.
summary: The BenQ ScreenBar Halo 2 is the best monitor light bar for gaming, with independent front and back lighting, a wireless dial and a motion sensor. The Quntis PRO+ is the best front light for ultrawides. Govee's G1 syncs backlight color to the screen, Razer's Aether suits Chroma setups, and several Quntis bars cover curved, RGB and budget needs.
intro: Light bars solve two separate problems, and shoppers who buy one expecting the other end up disappointed. A front light throws a clean, shadowless pool onto the keyboard and desk without bouncing off the screen. A backlight glows on the wall behind the monitor, softening the jump between a bright panel and a dark room, which is what tired eyes notice during a late session.

Few bars do both properly, and the cheaper ones nearly always handle only the first. We ranked nine, from plain desk lamps to RGB and screen-sync models, on paper. The order starts with how well each covers the two jobs, then moves to curved-monitor fit, controls and ecosystem integration. Colorful effects came last, because a colorful bar that leaves your desk dark is still a failed lamp.

products.name: BenQ ScreenBar Halo 2, Backlight, Wireless Dial, Motion Sensor
products.verdict: Independent front and back lighting with a wireless dial and motion sensor.
products.description:
BenQ's ScreenBar Halo 2 is the only bar here that does both jobs without compromise. A front light covers the desk, and a rear backlight softens the contrast with the wall, each with its own brightness control. It powers over USB-C, adds a wireless dial and a motion sensor, lists CRI 95 and fits curved monitors from 1000R to 1800R.

It wins because the two lights are independent: in a dark room you can lower the desk light and keep the glow, or the reverse. The Quntis models match it on front light but handle the backlight less cleanly.

Buy it for a dark room where eye strain is the issue. The caveat is that its backlight is a white-light bias effect, not a color show, and it costs more than the Quntis bars. Skip it if you want RGB.

products.name: Quntis Monitor Light Bar PRO+, 20-inch, Remote, 1200 Lux
products.verdict: A 20 inch bar with 1200 lux, auto-dimming and a wireless remote.
products.description:
The Quntis PRO+ is the strongest front light in the group. It is 20 inches long with 1200 lux output, a wireless remote, auto-dimming and CRI 95, and it is compatible with curved monitors. The 1200 lux figure is the highest output in the Quntis range, and a long bar is what an ultrawide needs.

It ranks second because it does the first job best: bright, glare-free desk light across a wide screen. What it lacks is a rear glow, which is the half of the job the Halo 2 adds.

Buy it for an ultrawide desk where a keyboard and notes need strong light. The caveat is that it gives plain white light only and no backlight. If you game in a dark room, pair it with a separate bias light or choose the BenQ.
products.idealFor: Ultrawide desks that need bright light.

products.name: Govee Gaming Light for Monitor G1, RGBIC LED, Screen Color Sync
products.verdict: The only pick that syncs backlight color to the screen, with 123 scenes.
products.description:
Govee's G1 is the immersive pick. It uses RGBIC LEDs with screen color sync, so the rear glow changes with what is on the monitor, plus 123 scene modes, music sync and app control, for monitors from 27 to 34 inches. Because RGBIC lets segments show different colors at once, the effect looks smoother than a single flat color.

It ranks third because screen sync is unique here, but it is a backlight, not a desk light. It does not replace a front bar, so you may need a second lamp for the keyboard.

Buy it for colorful gaming setups where atmosphere matters more than desk illumination. The caveat is dependence on the app: much of its value sits in software, and anyone who wants to light the desk should look at the BenQ or Quntis bars instead.
products.skipIf: You want to light your desk.

products.name: Razer Aether Monitor LED Light Bar, Chroma RGB, Front and Back
products.verdict: Chroma RGB with front and back lighting and Razer Synapse integration.
products.description:
Razer's Aether is the ecosystem bar. It offers Chroma RGB with 16.8 million colors, front and back lighting, Alexa compatibility, Razer Synapse integration and the Razer Gamer Room app. That software layer lets lighting react to games and sync with other Razer devices on the desk.

It ranks fourth because it matches the Halo 2 on having both front and back light, but its value is concentrated among owners of other Razer gear. Without that, you pay for integration you do not use.

Buy it if your keyboard, mouse or headset already runs on Chroma. The caveat is that full use needs the software installed, so if you do not own any Razer hardware, the BenQ Halo 2 gives better lighting for the same purpose without the dependency.

products.name: BenQ ScreenBar Pro, Motion Sensor, USB-C, 1000 Lux
products.verdict: 1000 lux, an ultrasonic motion sensor and a wireless dial, powered by USB-C.
products.description:
The ScreenBar Pro is BenQ's front-light version. It lists 1000 lux, an ultrasonic motion sensor, USB-C power at 19.7W, a wireless dial and curved monitor support from 1000R to 1800R. The motion sensor turns the bar on when you sit down and off when you leave, which saves the habit of remembering.

It ranks fifth because it is the Halo 2 without the backlight: the same dial and sensor, minus the rear glow, so there is nothing for a dark wall. As a desk light it still beats the RGB models for clean illumination.

Choose it for a bright, tidy desk glow with no color effects. The caveat is that it has no rear lighting and costs more than the Quntis bars, so Quntis PRO+ delivers more lux and more length for ultrawides if budget matters.
pros: Motion sensor auto on and off

products.name: Quntis Curved RGB Monitor Light Bar, Dual Head Foldable
products.verdict: A foldable dual-head mount for 1000R to 1800R curved monitors.
products.description:
The Quntis Curved is made for 1000R to 1800R curved monitors. It is a foldable dual-head bar with 15 RGB backlight modes, a remote and CRI 98 plus, sized for screens of 34 inches and up. Folding heads wrap around the bezel instead of sliding down a curve the way a rigid bar can.

It ranks sixth because the dual-head design is for a specific monitor type, and it gives both front light and RGB rear glow. For flat screens it adds complexity and cost without benefit.

Buy it for a curved ultrawide where a standard bar will not sit stable. The caveat is fit in the other direction: it suits large screens, so on a flat panel or a small monitor the Quntis PRO+ or the plain lamp is the better call.

products.name: Quntis RGB Pro+ Monitor Light Bar, 20-inch, 15 RGB Modes
products.verdict: A 20 inch bar with 15 RGB modes, 144 LEDs and a wireless remote.
products.description:
The Quntis RGB Pro+ stretches the long format into color. It is 20 inches with 15 RGB backlight modes, 144 LEDs, a wireless remote, CRI 95 and four color temperatures. The four temperature settings let you move from warm to cool light for the desk, not just rotate through colors.

It ranks seventh because it adds RGB to the ultrawide format, but its effects are simple next to Govee's sync. You choose a mode and live with it, and nothing follows the picture.

Buy it for an ultrawide gaming desk where you want color without an app. The caveat is plain effects, with no screen sync, so if the point is immersion, Govee's G1 is the better fit. It also gives less front light than the PRO+ at 1200 lux.

products.name: Quntis Computer Monitor Lamp, 900 Lux, Touch Control
products.verdict: 900 lux with an auto-dimming sensor and CRI 98 at a low price.
products.description:
The Quntis computer monitor lamp is the plain desk light. It lists 900 lux, an auto-dimming sensor, touch control, CRI 98 and USB power, with no screen glare. CRI 98 ties for the highest color accuracy in the group, which helps when you read papers or match colors under it.

It ranks eighth because there is no remote, RGB or backlight, only a lamp. It is the cheapest way to light a desk, and a better one than many RGB bars, but it does not add atmosphere to a gaming setup.

Buy it as a budget desk light when the goal is a lit keyboard, not a lit room. The caveat is that it is a lamp rather than a gaming light, with touch control only, so you reach for it directly. Step up to the PRO+ for remote control.

products.name: Quntis Monitor Light Bar, 15.7-inch, 24 RGB Backlight Modes
products.verdict: A 15.7 inch bar with 24 RGB modes and 900 lux front light.
products.description:
The 15.7 inch Quntis bar is the cheapest way into RGB. It offers 24 RGB backlight modes, 900 lux front light, touch control, CRI 95 and USB power. Twenty-four modes is the most of any Quntis here, and the shorter body fits the front of a smaller monitor.

It ranks last because length limits the spread: at 15.7 inches, it is too short for large monitors and ultrawides, and touch control means no remote. It remains the cheapest route to colored backlighting.

Buy it for a small gaming monitor on a tight budget. The caveat is the short bar, so check your monitor width, and skip it if you own an ultrawide, where the 20 inch bars light the whole desk.

whatMatters.detail: A front light puts glare-free light on your desk and keyboard. A backlight glows on the wall behind the screen and reduces contrast in a dark room. Decide which problem you have first, since it shapes the whole purchase: tired eyes in the dark call for a backlight, while a dim desk calls for a front light. The Halo 2 covers both.

A 15.7 inch bar suits a smaller screen, while a 20 inch bar suits an ultrawide. A bar shorter than the monitor leaves the ends of the desk dim and uneven, and one that is too long may not clamp. Check your monitor width and the listed bar length before ordering, since the bars here vary by about five inches.

Curved screens can make a rigid mount slide or tilt. Look for a listed curvature range such as 1000R to 1800R, which the BenQ bars and the Quntis Curved list. A foldable dual-head bar follows the curve of the bezel, and a flat monitor does not need that complexity.

Lux measures brightness, from 900 to 1200 among these bars, and CRI measures color accuracy, 95 to 98 here. A higher lux helps you read keys in a dark room, and higher CRI helps colors look natural on the desk. Find both numbers on the listing, not only the watt rating.

A wireless dial or remote avoids reaching behind the monitor, and motion sensors turn the bar off when you leave. Touch controls sit on the bar itself, so you reach up to the bar each time. Pick the control that matches how you sit and play: if you adjust lighting often during a session, a dial or remote is worth the extra cost.

faq.a: It is a soft light behind the screen that cuts the contrast between the bright panel and a dark wall, which eases eye strain in long evening sessions. The BenQ Halo 2 and Razer Aether provide it with a dedicated rear light.

faq.q: Will a light bar fit a curved monitor?
faq.a: Some do. The BenQ ScreenBar Pro and Halo 2 list 1000R to 1800R, and the Quntis Curved is built for those monitors with a foldable dual head. Check the curvature range before ordering, as flat-mount bars can slip.

Lux measures brightness. The Quntis PRO+ lists 1200 lux, the highest here, while the Quntis lamp and 15.7 inch bar list 900. Higher output helps in a dark room, but placement and angle matter just as much as the number.
For full effects on the Govee G1 and Razer Aether, yes. BenQ and Quntis bars use a dial, remote or touch control, so they work without any app or account, which keeps setup quick.

faq.q: Does a light bar cause screen glare?
faq.a: Well-designed bars aim light at the desk, not the screen. The Quntis lamp lists no screen glare, and the BenQ front lights are designed to avoid reflecting off the panel, so check your monitor surface.
The 20 inch Quntis PRO+ and RGB Pro+ cover ultrawides, and the Quntis Curved suits 34 inch and larger curved screens. The 15.7 inch bar is too short for them and leaves the desk ends dim.

finalTake: Buy the BenQ Halo 2 for a dark gaming room that needs both jobs done, or the Quntis PRO+ if you only want strong front light on an ultrawide. Pick the Govee G1 for screen sync, the Razer Aether if you own Chroma gear, and the Quntis Curved for 34 inch curved screens. Leave the cheapest RGB bar for small monitors.
